# ui::InsetWell

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Theme.hpp`.

A recessed well inside an indicator's border, as in Aero's check box and radio button. Their 13x13 glyphs have five layers, and the border and the flat fill are only the outer two. `rim` fills the shape `inset` in from the outer edge and `fill` the shape a pixel further in, so the rim shows as a 1px ring around the fill. With the default inset the rim covers `(2.5, 2.5, w-5, h-5)` and the fill `(3, 3, w-6, h-6)`. Both layers are filled, since their gradients run diagonally and only fills follow [`GradientAxis`](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#gradientaxis). [`draw_control_chrome`](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#draw_control_chrome) draws the well square, for the check box, and [RadioButton](../controls/radio-button.md#uiradiobutton) draws the same two layers round.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rim` | `LinearGradientBrush` |  | The outer layer, filling the shape `inset` in from the indicator's edge. |
| `fill` | `std::optional<LinearGradientBrush>` |  | The inner layer. Empty where the era skips it: a disabled Aero box keeps the rim and drops the fill. |
| `inset` | `float` | `2.0f` | DIPs from the indicator's outer edge to the rim. The fill starts one pixel further in. |
